mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressure, prompting the Fed to raise interest rates, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month signals strong economic growth, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 50% of instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 5% MoM signals weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where RSAFS declines by more than 5%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% MoM signals strengthening supply-side activity, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of instances where INDPRO increases by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% in a quarter signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in 3 months signals weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 5% each in a month signals strong demand, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 50% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS increase by more than 5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 2% YoY, it signals a restrictive monetary policy in a low-growth environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: restrictive monetary policy in low-growth environment
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 2% and GDPC1 YoY < 2%.
